draft.title: The spinal reflex
card: A spinal reflex is a fast, automatic response to a stimulus. It is carried out by a short pathway through the spinal cord.
Sensory neuron
carries the signal from a receptor, such as one in the skin, into the spinal cord.
Interneuron
sits in the spinal cord. It receives the signal from the sensory neuron and passes it on to a motor neuron.
Motor neuron
carries the signal out to a muscle, which contracts so the body pulls away. The brain is told at the same time, but the movement has usually started before pain is felt.
draft.remember: A reflex goes sensory neuron, interneuron, motor neuron, and the body moves before the brain registers pain.

a.q: Which sequence shows the path of a signal in a spinal reflex?
opts: Sensory neuron, interneuron, motor neuron
Motor neuron, interneuron, sensory neuron
Sensory neuron, brain, motor neuron
Interneuron, sensory neuron, motor neuron
a.why: The signal enters along a sensory neuron, is passed on by an interneuron in the spinal cord, then leaves along a motor neuron to the muscle. Going through the brain is tempting, but a reflex does not wait for the brain to act.
a.clue: The signal goes in, is passed on in the spinal cord, then goes out.

b.q: Jamal's hand touches a hot pan in a kitchen in Geelong and he jerks it away. Why can the hand move before he feels pain?
opts: An interneuron links the two neurons in the spinal cord
The sensory neuron waits for the brain to decide first
The motor neuron detects the heat and signals the muscle
The brain blocks pain until the hand has moved away
b.why: The interneuron in the spinal cord links the sensory neuron to the motor neuron, so the muscle is signalled without waiting for the brain. The brain is not the first step, so the movement can start before pain is registered.
b.clue: Which neuron links the incoming signal to the outgoing one?

b.best: An interneuron links the two neurons in the spinal cord
